newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal banks unperforming loans continue decline.
newsitem.headline: Portugal banks unperforming loans continue decline.

text.p: Unperforming loans and unpaid interest owed to Portuguese banks fell 1.3 percent year-on-year in the first half of 1996, continuing a downward trend, the Bank of Portugal said in its latest economic report.

The bank said the amount of unperforming loans and unpaid interest stood at 653.1 billion escudos ($4.3 billion) on June 30. Loans granted during the first six months rose 10.5 percent to 10.951 trillion escudos. Provisions against unperforming loans rose 6.1 percent to 433.1 billion escudos, while provisions against general credit risk fell 36.2 percent to 127.1 billion.
The bank said that the average solvency ratio of the banking system at the end of June stood at 12.2 percent, well above the eight percent legal minimum and up from 11.6 percent a year ago.
The rate of growth in individual credit continued high at 23.5 percent, reaching 3.9 trillion escudos. Housing loans were up 22 percent at 3.1 billion.
Loans to non-financial companies rose 6.5 percent to 5.43 trillion.
